claim.claim-text: 1. A method for scheduling Uplink (UL) data, characterized in that the method comprises:

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the beam information is an index of Sounding Reference Signal (SRS) resources, and/or the UL channel is a Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH) or a Physical Uplink Control Channel (PUCCH).
3. The method of claim 1 or 2, wherein performing (230), by the terminal device, carrier sensing on all or part of beams of the M beams according to the first signaling comprises:

performing, by the terminal device, carrier sensing on the M beams in sequence according to the first signaling until it is sensed on an Nth beam that a channel is idle, N being a positive integer less than or equal to M; and wherein selecting (240), by the terminal device, one of the all or part of beams according to the sensing result to send the UL channel to the network device comprises: sending, by the terminal device, the UL channel to the network device through the Nth beam.

4. The method of claim 3, wherein performing, by the terminal device, carrier sensing on the M beams in sequence according to the first signaling comprises: performing, by the terminal device, according to priorities of the M beams, carrier sensing on the M beams one by one in a sequence from high to low priorities.

5. The method of claim 3 or 4, wherein N beams which comprise the Nth beam and on which carrier sensing is performed correspond to N sensing windows one to one, and a sensing window used by the terminal device to perform carrier sensing on each beam of the N beams is the sensing window corresponding to the beam; wherein the N sensing windows are N successive sensing windows.
6. The method of any one of claims 1-5, wherein the UL channel is the PUSCH, and the first signaling further comprises information of a first time length,

the first time length being a time length between a slot, a starting time-domain symbol or an ending time-domain symbol where a Physical Downlink Control Channel (PDCCH) sent to the terminal device by the network device is located and a starting time point of a first sensing window, and the first sensing window being a sensing window which corresponds to a beam sensed firstly of the N beams, and/or wherein the UL channel is the PUSCH, and the first signaling further comprises information of a second time length, the second time length being a time length between a slot or an ending time-domain symbol where the PUSCH sent to the network device by the terminal device is located and a slot or a starting time-domain symbol where a downlink feedback channel is located, and the downlink feedback channel being configured for the terminal device to send feedback response information for the PUSCH to the network device.
7. A method for scheduling Uplink (UL) data, characterized in that the method comprises:

sending (210), by a network device, first signaling to a terminal device, the first signaling comprising beam information of M beams, M being a positive integer; and receiving (250), by the network device, a UL channel which is sent by the terminal device through one of the M beams.

8. The method of claim 7, wherein the beam information is an index of Sounding Reference Signal (SRS) resources, and/or the UL channel is a Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH) or a Physical Uplink Control Channel (PUCCH).
9. The method of claim 7 or 8, wherein receiving (250), by the network device, the UL channel which is sent by the terminal device through one of the M beams comprises:

receiving, by the network device, the UL channel which is sent by the terminal device through an Nth beam of the M beams, the Nth beam being a beam on which the terminal device senses that a channel is idle when performing carrier sensing on the M beams in sequence, and N being a positive integer less than or equal to M; wherein N beams which comprise the Nth beam and on which carrier sensing is performed correspond to N sensing windows one to one, and a sensing window used by the terminal device to perform carrier sensing on each beam of the N beams is the sensing window corresponding to the beam.
10. A terminal device, characterized in that the terminal device comprises:

a transceiver unit (610), configured to receive first signaling sent by a network device, the first signaling comprising beam information of M beams, M being a positive integer; and a sensing unit (620), configured to perform carrier sensing on the M beams in sequence according to the first signaling, wherein the transceiver unit (610) is further configured to select one of the M beams according to a sensing result to send an Uplink (UL) channel to the network device.

11. The terminal device of claim 10, wherein the beam information is an index of Sounding Reference Signal (SRS) resources, and/or the UL channel is a Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH) or a Physical Uplink Control Channel (PUCCH), and/or wherein the sensing unit (620) is specifically configured to:

perform carrier sensing on the M beams in sequence according to the first signaling until it is sensed on an Nth beam that a channel is idle, N being a positive integer less than or equal to M; and wherein the transceiver unit is specifically configured to send the UL channel to the network device through the Nth beam.
12. The terminal device of claims 10 or 11, wherein the sensing unit (620) is specifically configured to:
13. The terminal device of claim 12, wherein the UL channel is the PUSCH, and the first signaling further comprises information of a first time length,

the first time length being a time length between a slot, a starting time-domain symbol or an ending time-domain symbol where a Physical Downlink Control Channel (PDCCH) sent to the terminal device by the network device is located and a starting time point of a first sensing window, and the first sensing window being a sensing window which corresponds to a beam sensed firstly of the N beams, and/or wherein the UL channel is the PUSCH, and the first signaling further comprises information of a second time length, the second time length being a time length between a slot or an ending time-domain symbol where the PUSCH sent to the network device by the terminal device is located and a slot or a starting time-domain symbol where a downlink feedback channel is located, and the downlink feedback channel being configured for the terminal device to send feedback response information for the PUSCH to the network device.
14. A network device, characterized in that the network device comprises:

a transceiver unit (710), configured to send first signaling to a terminal device, the first signaling comprising beam information of M beams, M being a positive integer, wherein the transceiver unit (710) is further configured to receive an Uplink (UL) channel which is sent by the terminal device through one of the M beams.

15. The network device of claim 14, wherein the beam information is an index of Sounding Reference Signal (SRS) resources, and/or the UL channel is a Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH) or a Physical Uplink Control Channel (PUCCH), and/or wherein the transceiver unit (710) is specifically configured to:

receive the UL channel which is sent by the terminal device through an Nth beam of the M beams, the Nth beam being a beam on which the terminal device senses that a channel is idle when performing carrier sensing on the M beams in sequence, and N being a positive integer less than or equal to M; wherein N beams which comprise the Nth beam and on which carrier sensing is performed correspond to N sensing windows one to one, and a sensing window used by the terminal device to perform carrier sensing on each beam of the N beams is the sensing window corresponding to the beam.
